findings.summary: A worker that never settles boot can retain one of two module-global parser slots indefinitely; two such workers can leave parsing permanently busy until process restart.
acceptance: slot release is idempotent and has a terminal deadline independent of worker ready
two never-ready workers do not prevent a later valid parse without process restart
abort, error, exit, ready and timeout races release exactly once

findings.summary: Documents up to 20 MiB are structured-cloned into a worker and PDF bytes are copied again with slice; two global workers are allowed without a measured RSS budget.
acceptance: measure peak RSS with two maximum-size PDF and DOCX operations
prove cancellation and capacity recovery
remove avoidable copies or document and enforce a safe memory budget

findings.summary: The import-admit route buffers and parses approximately 16 MiB multipart before ui/human admission; the product router runs before general application authentication.
acceptance: unauthorized requests are rejected before full body materialization
bound total bytes, part count, concurrency and slow-upload duration
stress without session does not degrade authenticated traffic or create side effects

findings.scope: SQLite and request availability during backup
findings.summary: Backup capture retains a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction while copying, syncing, verifying and pruning files; queued store transactions use a default five-second deadline.
acceptance: external filesystem IO is not performed under a long business write lock
snapshot and blobs remain generation-consistent
realistic backup causes no Local storage lock timeout in concurrent GET and POST traffic

findings.summary: Timer ticks during an active cycle set pending and cause an immediate rerun; cycles longer than the interval can keep maintenance running continuously.
acceptance: missed ticks are coalesced without immediate infinite catch-up
explicit backoff and next-run policy are tested with cycles longer than the interval

findings.summary: Each cycle lists archives twice per surface and each list fully verifies snapshots and every retained blob, making recurring cost proportional to total retained bytes.
acceptance: inventory does not rehash all retained bytes every cycle
full verification has an explicit cadence, budget and cursor
cost is measured through 84 monthly archives per surface

findings.summary: list and prune convert any archive load error into absence, so corrupt archives can disappear from inventory, evade prune and remain invisible to maintenance health.
acceptance: distinguish missing archives from corruption
surface corruption and orphaned bytes in health
quarantine or custody-safe remediation is explicit

findings.scope: backup disk exhaustion after abrupt process loss
findings.summary: An abrupt crash can leave a nearly complete .stage-* directory; list and prune only recognize backup-* names and no stage scavenger exists in the backup module.
acceptance: subprocess kill is tested between durable writes, verify and rename
restart discovers and safely quarantines or removes stale owned stages
orphaned bytes are observable

findings.summary: jobs.dispose and store.dispose await active operations, while backup capture has no cancellation signal; slow or stuck filesystem IO can extend shutdown without a bounded deadline.
acceptance: define a safe cancellation point and shutdown deadline
systemd stop during each backup phase leaves no partial publication or stuck lock
restart behavior is proven

testCoverageObservations: No dedicated never-ready parser worker and two-slot recovery test was identified in the inspected test inventory.
local-backups.test.ts uses a four-byte retained blob and does not exercise realistic IO latency or concurrent request timeouts.
local-jobs.test.ts uses a three-byte blob and schedule=false, so it does not exercise real timer overlap or catch-up behavior.
No adversarial maximum multipart without-session concurrency benchmark was identified in this review.
